source: NCERT-aligned UPSC Ecology & Environment (Class XI), Ch. 3 (Biodiversity: Concepts, Patterns and Hotspots).

sections.heading: 1. What is Biodiversity?
points: **Biodiversity** (term popularised by **E.O. Wilson**) = the variety of life at all levels.

sub: **Genetic diversity** — variation of genes within a species.
**Species diversity** — variety of species in a region.

points: Biodiversity is highest near the **equator (tropics)** and decreases toward the poles (latitudinal gradient).

sections.heading: 2. Importance of Biodiversity
points: **Ecosystem services** — pollination, climate regulation, nutrient cycling, water purification, soil formation.
**Economic value** — food, medicine, timber, resources.
**Ecological stability** and resilience; ethical and aesthetic value.
India is a **megadiverse country** (one of 17 in the world).

sections.heading: 3. Biodiversity Hotspots
points: A **biodiversity hotspot** (concept by **Norman Myers**) = a region with **high endemism (≥1500 endemic plant species)** AND **high threat (≥70% of original habitat lost)**.
There are ~**36 hotspots** globally.
India has **four hotspots**: **the Himalayas, the Western Ghats & Sri Lanka, the Indo-Burma region, and Sundaland (Nicobar Islands)**.
**Endemic species** = found only in a particular area.

sections.heading: 4. Threats to Biodiversity
points: **The 'Evil Quartet'**: **habitat loss/fragmentation, over-exploitation, invasive alien species, and co-extinctions**.
Pollution and **climate change** add to the threats.
Loss of biodiversity reduces ecosystem services and stability.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Three levels: genetic, species, ecosystem diversity; term = E.O. Wilson.
Biodiversity highest near the equator (tropics).
Hotspot = high endemism (≥1500 endemic plants) + ≥70% habitat lost (Norman Myers).
India's 4 hotspots: Himalayas, Western Ghats & Sri Lanka, Indo-Burma, Sundaland.
'Evil Quartet': habitat loss, over-exploitation, invasive species, co-extinctions.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: Three levels of biodiversity: **genetic, species, ecosystem**.
A **hotspot** needs BOTH **high endemism AND high threat (≥70% habitat lost)**.
India has **four biodiversity hotspots** (Himalaya, Western Ghats-Sri Lanka, Indo-Burma, Sundaland).
**Endemic** = restricted to one area (unique to it).
